title: Strings in Depth
summary: Characters as numbers and the Character class, walking through strings, why repeated concatenation is slow and how StringBuilder fixes it, string comparison and sorting, splitting with regular expressions, a first look at Pattern and Matcher, and converting between strings, chars and numbers.

cards.q: Why build a long string in a loop with `StringBuilder` rather than `+=`?
cards.a:
Strings are immutable, so `+=` copies the whole string every time; `StringBuilder` appends in place

Each `+=` creates a brand-new string and copies everything so far, which is quadratic in a loop. A `StringBuilder` is a mutable buffer you append to.

7, because the codes of `'0'` to `'9'` are consecutive

Arithmetic on chars works on their codes, and the digit codes are in order. `'7'` is 55 and `'0'` is 48, so the difference is the digit's value, 7.

`["a", "b", "c"]`

The runs of digits are the separators and are not kept; the trailing empty piece after "333" is dropped.
